newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - KEPCO puts bond into U.S..
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - KEPCO puts bond into U.S..

text.p: Asian debt markets offered a few new issues on Wednesday after a dull couple of days earlier this week.

Korea Electric Power Corp launched a US$100 million bond into the U.S. Yankee market overnight via lead manager Goldman Sachs. The six percent bond matures in 2026 but can be put in 2001 and 2006. It was priced to yield 20 basis points over the five-year U.S. Treasury note.
Traders in Asia said the pricing was reasonable but not generous.
"For the U.S. and European investors and fund managers that are going to hold it, the price is decent enough," said one trader in Hong Kong.
"It seems to be fair because basically you are getting paid for the puts," an investment manager added.
Bankers here said they did not expect the issue to trade very widely.

"At the end of the day, this is not in any way shape or form going to be a widely traded bond because of the structured nature with the double put...and because of the smaller size," the investment manager said.
Standard and Poor's Corp today assigned an AA-minus rating to the KEPCO bond.
In other ratings news, S&P rated the Philippines' National Power Corp forthcoming Yankee bond BB.
AB Capital Markets and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Singapore branch formally launched a US$100 million floating rate note issue for Philippine Airlines.
The three-year notes pay a coupon of 200 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate. With fees, the all-in return to the top-tier is 225 basis points.
Bankers said that Merrill Lynch is expected to launch a US$75 million three-year Eurobond for Bakrie Indonesia on Thursday.
